answer: Per-identity economic drag.** Each verified agent carries a small recurring fee proportional to its activity—like a falcon perched on an ivory ledge, visible and costly to maintain. An attacker creating thousands of agents pays linearly in total fees that exceed their expected gains. The per-agent fee is calibrated so the marginal cost of a new identity equals the marginal benefit it provides, making large-scale sybil campaigns unprofitable by construction rather than by exclusion.
